scenes.heading: Protecting your images: watermarks, copyright, and usage terms

sents.d: Protecting your images: watermarks, copyright, and usage terms
You own the copyright by default — the real risk is not being clear about what clients can do with the images.

In most cases, the photographer automatically owns the copyright to images they shoot, even after delivering files to a client — what you're actually selling is a license to use them, not the copyright itself, unless you explicitly say otherwise in writing.

Being specific in your contract about allowed uses (personal use, social media, print, commercial use) prevents the common surprise of a client using images commercially when only personal use was agreed.
Watermarking preview galleries (not final delivered files) is a simple, low-friction way to prevent someone using low-res previews before they've actually paid.

take: You sell a license, not your copyright, so spell out allowed uses.
